approaches.fromDirection: This approach comes from the west, across open fringe ground.
approaches.sequence: The two towers come into view first. The gate between them opens onto the way. The houses stand east along the way.
approaches.wayfinding: Travellers walk east along the way. They pass through the gate in the wall run.

approaches.sequence: The raft and the landing stage come into view first. The boardwalk and the stilt house follow up the beach.
approaches.wayfinding: Travellers step off the raft. They walk north-west along the landing stage onto the way.

causalModel.founding: Yard B is a fixture of ten test cells. The cells were laid out in the placement workbench. They are built to compare with the first yard.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Yard B has no occupants and no lore.
causalModel.pressures: Yard B is a fixture. It is never part of the shipped game.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The site is empty fringe ground falling gently east. It reaches open sea deep enough for the raft within 15 m of the beach.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The fixture changes if a kit piece under test changes. It changes if the runtime contract moves. It changes if the workbench is retired.

combatSpaces.why: The ground along the way through yard B is kept open. The open ground serves the animation tests.

districts.notes: Test cells for the imperial kit set.

why.what: The imperial group is a part of yard B. It holds the wall run, the farmhouse, the sign post and the sconce wall.
why.whyHere: The imperial group sits on empty fringe ground at the west end of yard B. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whyNeighbours: The imperial group keeps to one kit set. A kit-purity warning in yard B therefore reads as a real one.
why.playerPurpose: The imperial group has no purpose in the game. It proves the imperial kit set and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground at the west end of yard B is level fringe ground. Each cell is under the plinth or pad limit.

districts.notes: Test cells for the argonian-stilt kit set.

why.what: The stilt group is a part of yard B. It holds the two huts, the boardwalk run, the landing stage and the raft.
why.whyHere: The stilt group sits on empty ground running down to the sea. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whyNeighbours: The stilt group keeps to the argonian-stilt kit set. A kit-purity warning therefore reads as a real one.
why.playerPurpose: The stilt group has no purpose in the game. It proves the stilt kit set and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is fringe ground falling east. It runs down to the beach and the open sea.

districts.notes: Test cells for the argonian-root kit set.

why.what: The root group is a part of yard B. It holds only the dug-in cave mouth.
why.whyHere: The root group sits on empty fringe ground north of the way. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whyNeighbours: The cave mouth keeps its own kit set apart. A kit-purity warning therefore reads as a real one.
why.playerPurpose: The root group has no purpose in the game. It proves the argonian-root kit set and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is sloping fringe ground north of the way. It falls south.

landmarks.notes: Mounted child of the sign-post piece by its mined mount pair.

why.what: The sign is a test piece. It is the Drunken Huntsman board. The board hangs from the Whiterun sign post in yard B.
why.whyHere: The sign is a fixture. It proves that a board hangs from its post at Bethesda's own offset.
why.whySpot: The board hangs under the arm of the post. It sits at the offset that Bethesda's own two placements of this pair use.
why.whyNeighbours: The board hangs from the sign post beside the way. The post stands just inside the gate of yard B.
why.playerPurpose: The hanging sign has no purpose in the game. It proves a mounted piece in yard B and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The board hangs about 2.4 m above level ground. It hangs under the arm of the post.

landmarks.notes: Mounted child of the sconce-wall piece by its mined mount pair.

why.what: The sconce is a test piece. It is a candle sconce. It hangs on the free-standing imperial wall panel in yard B.
why.whyHere: The sconce is a fixture. It proves that a light hangs on a wall at a mined offset.
why.whySpot: The sconce hangs on the face of the panel. It sits at the offset that Bethesda's own placements of this pair use most often.
why.whyNeighbours: The sconce hangs on the sconce wall panel. The panel is 13 m from the sign post in yard B.
why.playerPurpose: The sconce has no purpose in the game. It proves a hung light in yard B and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The sconce hangs about 2.7 m up the face of the panel. The panel stands above level ground.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall run stands roughly north to south across the west end of the way. The gate arch lets the way pass east into the yard.

why.what: The test run is imperial-wall-run. It has five curtain-wall pieces from the Morrowind keep set. The pieces are laid in the workbench on the joints that its plugins use. A broken wall stands at each end.
why.whyHere: The wall run is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The site is a strip about 35 m long west of the yard. Every cell under each piece is under 2 deg.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall run stands alone at the west end. The sign post is 9.6 m east of it. The sconce wall is 18.6 m east of it.
why.playerPurpose: The wall run has no purpose in the game. It proves a run authored piece by piece in the workbench and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is level fringe ground. The steepest cell under any of the five pieces is 1.8 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The door of the farmhouse is on the south wall. The south wall faces the way. A short footpath joins the door to the way.

why.what: The test piece is imperial-house. It is the farmhouse composite with the door leaf that Skyrim hangs on it. It is seated as a plinth.
why.whyHere: The farmhouse is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The farmhouse stands north of the way on ground where the plinth fit holds. There is 0.4 m of fall under the house. The ground at its door is level with the ground around it.
why.whyNeighbours: The farmhouse stands 22 m from the bamboo hut to its east. It stands 23 m from the wall run to its west.
why.playerPurpose: The farmhouse cell has no purpose in the game. It proves a plinth-seated building and its door and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is gently sloping fringe ground. There is 0.4 m of fall across the footprint. The stone plinth takes up the fall. The steepest cell is 3.8 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The sign post stands beside the way just inside the gate. Its board hangs over the verge.

why.what: The test piece is sign-post. It is the Whiterun sign post. It stands on its designed sink.
why.whyHere: The sign post is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The post stands beside the way. It is 3.5 m south of the way's centreline. It is clear of the gate arch.
why.whyNeighbours: The post is 9.6 m east of the wall run. The post is 13 m from the sconce wall.
why.playerPurpose: The sign post cell has no purpose in the game. It proves a post with a hanging board and is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is level fringe ground. The steepest cell under the post is 1.8 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall stands square to the way. Its candle sconce faces the walker.

why.what: The test piece is called sconce-wall. It is the free-standing imperial wall panel impfreewall01, which stands on its designed sink.
why.whyHere: The sconce wall is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The panel stands south of the way near the gate. The ground there is under 2 deg.
why.whyNeighbours: The panel is 13 m from the sign post. It is 18.6 m from the wall run.
why.playerPurpose: The sconce wall cell has no purpose in play. It proves a wall that carries a hung light. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground under the panel is level fringe ground. The steepest cell under the panel is 1.2 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut door faces south towards the way. A footpath joins the door to the way.

why.what: The test piece is called hut. It is the HTBM bamboo hut, seated on its legs. The hut carries the door leaf that the mod hangs on it at a fixed offset.
why.whyHere: The bamboo hut is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The hut stands north of the way. The ground there is under the 3 deg limit for a piece on legs.
why.whyNeighbours: The hut is 22 m east of the farmhouse. The stilt house is 52 m further east.
why.playerPurpose: The bamboo hut cell has no purpose in play. It proves a small hut on legs and its door. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground under the hut is level fringe ground. The steepest cell under the hut is 1.7 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open front of the stilt house faces north onto the way. A short footpath joins the front to the way.

why.what: The test piece is called stilt-hut. It is the BM&V stilt house composite. Its deck is held at the height that the mod's own placements use. Its legs are driven into the ground.
why.whyHere: The stilt house is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The stilt house stands south of the way. The ground there is under the 3 deg limit for a piece on legs.
why.whyNeighbours: The stilt house is 31 m from the cave mouth. It is 50 m from the boardwalk run.
why.playerPurpose: The stilt house cell has no purpose in play. It proves a deck seated above the ground on long legs. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground under the stilt house is level fringe ground. The steepest cell under the stilt house is 1.5 deg.

parcels.orientationWhy: The boardwalk run lies east to west beside the way near the shore. Its last plank is turned at the joint angle that HTBM uses for its own docks.

why.what: The test run is called boardwalk-run. It is three Kothringi plank docks from HTBM. The docks join on the paired joints that the mod uses. The run is a built way.
why.whyHere: The boardwalk run is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The run stands on low ground near the shore. Every cell under the planks is under the 3 deg limit for a piece on legs.
why.whyNeighbours: The boardwalk is 26 m from the landing stage. It is 29 m from the cave mouth.
why.playerPurpose: The boardwalk run has no purpose in play. It proves a built way laid piece by piece. The run is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground is low fringe ground a metre above the sea. The steepest cell under the planks is 2.6 deg.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The raft lies half a metre off the sea end of the landing stage. A walker steps from the deck onto the raft.
parcels.orientationWhy: The shore end of the landing stage meets the end of the way. Its deck runs south-east over the sea to the raft.

why.what: The test piece is called landing-stage. It is the docks-v1 quay run of two dock sections. The run goes from the beach out to the raft.
why.whyHere: The landing stage is a fixture. It carries the way from the beach out to water that is deep enough for the raft.
why.whySpot: The bank rises to the height of the deck at the water's edge. The stage starts on the shore and spans the shallows.
why.whyNeighbours: The ferry raft lies half a metre off the sea end of the stage. The boardwalk run is 26 m inland.
why.playerPurpose: The landing stage cell has no purpose in play. It proves a quay seated at sea level. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The shore end of the stage stands on dry beach. The rest of the run stands over open sea.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The raft is moored half a metre off the sea end of the landing stage. A walker can board the raft from the deck.
parcels.orientationWhy: The raft lies end on to the landing stage. It is in line with the stage deck.

why.what: The test piece is called hull-berth. It is the ferry raft ferryraft01. The raft floats at the recorded sea level.
why.whyHere: The raft is a fixture. It proves that a hull floats on at least a metre of water.
why.whySpot: The raft lies off the end of the landing stage. Every cell within 2.5 m of the raft holds at least 1.3 m of water. The seabed there is under 3 deg.
why.whyNeighbours: The raft lies half a metre off the sea end of the landing stage. The boardwalk run is 40 m to the north-west.
why.playerPurpose: The raft cell has no purpose in play. It proves a floating hull at a stage. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The raft lies in open sea at least 1.3 m deep. The water is that deep under and around the raft.

parcels.orientationWhy: The cave mouth is turned so that the ramp into it faces north. The ramp faces the way.

why.what: The test piece is called cave-mouth. It is the cave door frame doorcaveb. The frame is dug in so that its sill is flush with the ground in front of it.
why.whyHere: The cave mouth is a fixture on empty fringe ground. Its position has no lore reason.
why.whySpot: The cave mouth stands north of the way. The ground rises behind the frame, so the frame is dug into the slope.
why.whyNeighbours: The cave mouth is 31 m from the stilt house. It is 29 m from the boardwalk run.
why.playerPurpose: The cave mouth cell has no purpose in play. It proves a dug-in opening. The cell is not part of the game.
why.microGeography: The ground under the frame is sloping fringe ground. The steepest cell under the frame is 4.2 deg.

blueprint.partTwoTestSitesNote: Yard B holds no pad corner test sites. It holds no clearing or rock test sites either. Those test sites stay with the first yard.

routes.why: The way runs through yard B. It runs east from the gate in the wall run to the landing stage.
A footpath runs from the way to the farmhouse door. The door opens onto a walked line.
A footpath runs from the way to the stilt house front. The front door opens onto a walked line.
A footpath runs from the way to the bamboo hut door. The door opens onto a walked line.

scaleGrounding.why: Yard B has ten test cells. Each cell tests one mechanism. The cells are laid out in the workbench. Yard B has no population.
